transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Oliver (CTO), Priya (Lead ML), Sam (SRE), Dana (Procurement)

Summary: quick intake to size dedicated footprint, understand isolation requirements, burst patterns and fallback expectations; surface security and procurement constraints.

Topics covered: current infra, latency & cost targets, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC/KMS/SSO needs, warm-pool and prewarm strategies, benchmark next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, I'm Maya, I'm the account lead for Stonebridge. Ravi from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Oliver (CTO): Good, thanks. Running a little behind but all good.
[00:10] Priya (Lead ML): Morning—afternoon, yeah.
[00:12] Sam (SRE): Hi.
[00:14] Maya: Quick agenda, we'll do a brief about Redwood Dedicated, then gap/questions, then sizing and burst patterns, and finish with security/procurement asks and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:22] Oliver: Yep.
[00:24] Maya: Ravi, real quick high-level on how our Dedicated offering works in practice?
[00:28] Ravi (Redwood SE): Sure. So Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool you get—I mean you reserve capacity, it's isolated to your tenancy, and we provide autoscaling/burst options. The runtime does continuous batching, KV cache—sometimes transcribed as K V cash in older docs—but basically prefix caching to lower token cost. For heavy tail workloads we recommend warm-pools and pre-warm windows.
[00:53] Priya: When you say warm-pools, is that per-tenant reserve or a shared hot pool with tenancy fencing? We need hard isolation for PII workloads.
[01:01] Ravi: You can choose strict isolation—single-tenant nodes—or a hybrid where warm pools are dedicated but can be reclaimed per policy. There's also private on-prem packaging if you need all control. For PII, customers usually go Dedicated with single-tenant nodes plus KMS integration.
[01:19] Sam: What's the failure behavior during burst? If our traffic spikes 6x for a few minutes, do requests queue, fail, or get routed to a hosted fallback?
[01:28] Maya: Good question. You can configure a fallback policy: route to hosted compatible model, or degrade to a smaller quantized model, or return a 429. We typically design canary fallback paths—automatic until capacity recovers.
[01:37] Oliver: We want automatic fallback to hosted for non-sensitive calls but not for PII. So routing by tag would be great. Can Redwood route by request tag or token?
[01:46] Ravi: Yes, request-level routing by policy or tag is supported. You can also pin model versions per route. In practice, you set a policy: if request.metadata.sensitivity=="low" then allow hosted fallback.
[01:58] Priya: Sounds promising. Some of our models keep large KV caches—how do you handle cache persistence across rotations?
[02:05] Ravi: We persist KV per session where possible and also have sticky routing to keep KV locality. There are edge cases with preemption where KV is lost but we provide cold-start mitigations—partial recovery through checkpointed caches.
[02:18] Priya: Ok. For sizing, here's our quick picture: currently 3 services that call models: chat endpoints for customer support (p50 200ms, p95 1.2s), generation for batch summarization (p50 450ms), and an internal reranker. Peak QPS right now ~120 reqs/min but spikes to 700 reqs/min during incidents. Average token length varies 80–450 tokens.
[02:39] Maya: That's helpful. Do you have p99 latency targets or SLOs?
[02:42] Oliver: We want p95 under 1s for customer-facing chat and p99 under 2s ideally. Cost can't exceed our current spend by more than 25% on steady-state.
[02:51] Sam: Also want audit logs going back 90 days minimum and SSO integration.
[02:55] Maya: Noted. Let's capture requirements: p95 <1s chat; p99 <2s; 90d audit logs; SSO + SAML; KMS for key separation.
[03:03] Priya: For the burst profile—spikes are usually short, 3–8 minutes, heavy token volume. We don't want to overprovision for 1000 low-utility minutes. What are warm-pool prewarm times?
[03:12] Ravi: Depends on model and GPU. For A100/80GB with optimized kernels, warm-pool prewarm is roughly 30–60s to reach steady per-token throughput if caches are cold; with prefix cached it's faster. For quantized LLMs on T4-ish hardware it's longer.
[03:26] Priya: So the 3–8 minute spikes could be handled with a small warm pool plus a brief hosted fallback for certain routes.
[03:33] Oliver: Pricing question—do you price warm-pools differently from reserved nodes?
[03:36] Maya: Warm-pools are priced as reserved capacity with an operational premium; the addendum outlines burst units and per-minute billing for burst beyond reserved baseline. We'll share the sheet after the call.
[03:46] Dana (Procurement): On contracting, we need term options and a clause for surge credits if availability falls below SLA.
[03:52] Maya: We offer SLA-backed response and can discuss surge credits in enterprise agreements.
[03:56] Sam: Network topology—we need VPC peering and private link. Any egress to public internet for hosted fallback?
[04:02] Ravi: For Dedicated in VPC mode we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and you can opt-in for no egress—hosted fallback requires routing through Redwood's hosted endpoints unless you have Private (on-prem) deployment. But you can set policy to only fallback to private cluster if you spin one up.
[04:18] Priya: For encryption, KMS integration—customer-managed keys?
[04:21] Maya: Yep, we support customer KMS/HSM and envelope encryption; keys never leave your control.
[04:26] Priya: Good. Compliance—SOC 2 and ISO?
[04:29] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO-27001. I'll share the audit pack link.
[04:33] Oliver: Great. On benchmarking, we want a realistic sim that includes our token size distribution; can you replicate our traffic shapes?
[04:39] Ravi: We can run workload-driven benchmarks if you share traffic CSVs. We'll spin up a dedicated bench cluster that mirrors your reserve config (e.g., 4xA100 nodes) and run steady-state and spike tests. We'll measure latency at p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:55] Priya: What's the expected turnaround for a bench? We need something to evaluate by Oct 15th for our Q4 planning.
[04:59] Ravi: If we get data by Oct 2, we can run and deliver a report by Oct 9–12. That works with your Oct 15 deadline.
[05:06] Maya: I'll add that to next steps.
[05:09] Oliver: One more on tenancy: any noisy neighbor protection beyond node fencing? CPU/IO bandwidth reservations?
[05:16] Ravi: Yes, beyond node-level isolation we have QoS for IO and network shaping and tenant throttles. For strict isolation we recommend dedicated single-tenant nodes to avoid any shared kernel resources.
[05:26] Priya: Are there limits to model versions or custom kernels? We sometimes bring custom quantization kernels.
[05:31] Ravi: We support custom model artifacts and can onboard quantized variants; kernel work may require collaboration with our infra team. There's a safety review for custom kernels but it's possible.
[05:41] Sam: For monitoring—can we get token-level breakdowns per route and tracing hooks?
[05:45] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks you can forward to your observability stack. We'll include sample dashboards.
[05:55] Dana: For procurement process, what's the typical lead time for Dedicated contract and for node provisioning?
[06:01] Maya: Contract negotiation typical 2–4 weeks for enterprise terms; provisioning of reserved capacity after PO is about 7–14 days depending on region and GPU availability. For urgent cases we can discuss expedited timelines.
[06:12] Oliver: If we do a phased approach—start with 2 reserved nodes and expand—how does capacity expansion work? Can we burst beyond reserved instantly?
[06:19] Ravi: Yes, there's burst capacity that can draw from a shared pool; you can configure burst ceilings. But instant burst depends on region capacity; warm-pool prewarm helps. For immediate needs, hosted fallback is the quick answer.
[06:30] Priya: Ok that's workable.
[06:33] Maya: Any blockers re security or procurement that would stop you from piloting?
[06:38] Dana: We need the SOC2 pack, a draft contract with SLAs and indemnities, and a quote broken down by reserved nodes, warm-pool, and burst minutes. Also a data processing addendum.
[06:50] Maya: We'll provide those.
[06:52] Oliver: On price sensitivity—our steady-state cost target is not to exceed current infra spend by more than 25%. We'll need to see the numbers.
[06:59] Maya: Understood.
[07:01] Priya: For the bench, can you simulate our incident pattern where we see a sudden backend search storm? It trips up token backpressure in other systems.
[07:09] Ravi: Yep, we'll model a 6x spike for 5 minutes and measure fallback behavior. We'll also test prewarm sizes: 0, small (1 node), medium (2 nodes) warm-pools to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:22] Oliver: Good. One question: do you support per-request routing to on-prem private clusters? We might want to pass EU PII to a private cluster.
[07:30] Ravi: We support private deployments and can route requests via region or by tag to a private cluster. That requires network connectivity and deployment of the private runtime.
[07:38] Sam: If we go private in EU, what's the uplift?
[07:41] Maya: Private deployments have a platform fee plus infra; we can get finance to model that in the quote.
[07:47] Priya: Do you have RBAC that integrates with our IdP? We want least privilege for routes.
[07:52] Ravi: SSO/SAML with role mappings and fine-grained RBAC is supported; route-level RBAC is possible via policy tags.
[07:59] Oliver: Ok, I think we have the info to proceed. Any final clarifying questions?
[08:03] Priya: One more—are there anti-affinity controls to avoid placing our reserved nodes in the same failure domain?
[08:09] Ravi: Yes, we allow topology constraints and anti-affinity placement to reduce simultaneous failure risk.
[08:15] Maya: Great. Recap of next steps: Maya will send pricing + SOC2/ISO audit pack and draft contract; Ravi will prepare benchmark config and perf expectations; customer will share traffic shape and p95/p99 samples by Oct 2. We will tentatively schedule an SE deep-dive and bench kickoff week of Oct 5.
[08:34] Dana: Thanks.
[08:36] Oliver: Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

Notes / imperfections: occasional transcription glitches (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache; product name sometimes heard as "Redwood Allocate"), small crosstalk, filler words preserved.
